A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, and their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices can be reliably matched. Figure 23 overflows the page in both versions, but its embedded panels are recoverable and comparable.

before.justification: V1 reports original RNN experiments, concept decoding and intervention results in language models, and unsupervised chunk and POS-tag analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds quantitative grafting/freezing results and evaluations using ROCStories-derived concepts and TREC prompts.

M1.justification: DSC, PA, and UCD retain their algorithms, objectives, and extraction rules. Grafting still overwrites selected activations and freezing zeros them. The new intervention definitions and discussion of unsuccessful alternatives do not introduce components into the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds ROCStories for extracting concepts from naturalistic stories and TREC's six question categories for testing grafting across varied prompt contexts. This substantially broadens the earlier selected-prompt intervention coverage. The existing RNN, narrative-schema, frequent-word, and Emma evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Appendix F.1 adds qualitative assessments of tied-weight SAE-like reconstruction and binarized-hidden-state alternatives, reporting interpretability and training difficulties. The corresponding concept-decoding comparison retains the same pretrained Sparsify SAE; the expanded related-work discussion does not establish additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces systematic grafting evaluation using 2,000 ROCStories sentences, filtered frequent concepts, 50 TREC prompts per category, three intervention layer ranges, and concept-occurrence rates against control. Separately, the reported extraction procedure for the RNN-size comparison changes from UCD to DSC; the retained Figure 11 results do not establish that this experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds intervention sensitivity analyses across layers and prompt categories, and contrasts words with strong and weak grafting effects (Table 1; Appendix E.7). Appendix F.1 also reports unsuccessful architectural alternatives. The earlier RNN controls, hierarchy experiments, POS analyses, and dictionary-size sensitivity analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports N=100 generation trials for the fixed-prompt grafting/freezing estimates (Figure 3; Tables 3–4). The earlier ten-run RNN comparison and SEM reporting remain. No confidence intervals or new significance-testing procedure accompany the added intervention percentages.

E6.justification: V2 adds quantitative outcomes beyond v1's generated-text examples: cake occurrence is 1% without versus 83% with grafting, and cheese occurrence is 67% without versus 33% with freezing (Tables 3–4). Table 1 adds context/layer results, while Tables 5–6 report strong and weak word-specific effects. These are newly reported results, not performance gains over v1's retained decoding plots.

T1.justification: Section 3 introduces an explicit mathematical definition of a recurring input subsequence P, including variable lengths, and relates its activation trajectory to a population chunk. The existing SLLN statement, extraction equations, losses, and RNN equations remain; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the Reflection Hypothesis, the three extraction methods, concrete and abstract concept recovery across architectures, and causal intervention claims. V2's abstract explicitly names POS tags and narrative schemas, but these capabilities and findings were already present in v1.

C2.justification: V1 already warned that averaging could obscure contextual distinctions. V2 expands this into a semantic-prototype interpretation, discusses polysemy and function-word limitations using intervention results, and adds interpretations concerning distributed encoding, deeper-layer variability, and grafting versus freezing effectiveness (Appendices E.1, E.6–E.7).

D1.justification: V2 adds batch-size, epoch, memory, runtime, and scaling information in Appendix G, plus intervention details in E.6. Appendix I changes the hardware disclosure from A100 to Quadro RTX 6000, although the checklist still says A100. New checklist statements about supplied code/data and deferred asset release conflict, so actual availability is not established.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning against polytope methods, multidimensional concept subspaces, codebook features, and vision concept methods such as TCAV. It also develops comparisons with SAE steering/unlearning and representation engineering. Thirteen references are added while the earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, portions of the introduction and hypothesis exposition, and the conclusion. It substantially reorganizes the appendices: DSC pseudocode becomes a standalone section, PA/UCD validation is separated, PA exposition is divided into focused subsections, and UCD analyses and disclosure sections are reordered.

P2.justification: V2 adds intervention tables and embeds quantitative summaries in revised Figure 3, redraws Figure 11, moves v1's Figure 1 into the appendix as Figure 7, and rearranges UCD displays. Most figure content and the overall visual style are retained, including the shared Figure 23 overflow.

improvement.justification: V1's LLM intervention claim relied largely on selected generation examples. V2 substantially strengthens this central claim through quantified grafting/freezing trials, broader prompt-context testing, layer comparisons, and explicit weak-effect cases (Table 1; Tables 3–6). This makes intervention reliability and applicability boundaries much easier to assess. Missing uncertainty estimates and conflicting hardware/code disclosures limit reproducibility gains, but do not outweigh the stronger empirical support.
